topic: Solving Linear Inequalities and Number Line Representation

lessonData.topic: Solving Linear Inequalities and Number Line Representation
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Geometry
lessonData.tagline: Unlock infinite solutions and map continuous intervals with precision across the number line.
lessonData.overview: Solving a linear inequality produces a continuous set of infinitely many solutions rather than a single fixed value. By applying inverse operations, flipping the inequality symbol when dividing or multiplying by negative numbers, and choosing the correct boundary marker (open circle vs. solid dot), any solution range can be precisely visualized on a number line.

chalkNotes.title: Solving Linear Inequalities & Number Lines
chalkNotes.subtitle: Continuous Solution Sets and Boundary Rules
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: If ax < b and a < 0, then x > b/a. Boundary Rule: '<' or '>' = Open Circle (○); '<=' or '>=' = Solid Dot (●).
bulletPoints: Linear inequalities possess infinitely many solutions within continuous intervals on the real number line.
Apply identical inverse operations as linear equations, with one vital exception: reverse the inequality symbol when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
Open circles mean the boundary value is EXCLUDED; solid dots mean the boundary value is INCLUDED.
Always read with the variable on the left (e.g., rewrite 3 < x as x > 3) to accurately determine which direction to shade.
keyTakeaways: Never truncate a strict inequality to the previous integer: x < 5 includes 4.9, 4.99, and 4.999, which requires an open circle at 5, not a solid dot at 4.
The arrow points in the direction of the solution set, pointing right for greater-than (x > a) and left for less-than (x < a).

quiz.question: Solve the inequality 8 - x > 3 over the real numbers and identify how its solution must be represented on a number line.
options: x < 5; represented by an open circle at 5 with a continuous ray pointing to the left.
x < 5; represented by a solid dot at 4 with a ray pointing to the left, because 5 is not included.
x > 5; represented by an open circle at 5 with a continuous ray pointing to the right because the original sign was '>'.
x <= 5; represented by a solid dot at 5 with a continuous ray pointing to the left.
quiz.explanation: Subtracting 8 gives -x > -5. Dividing both sides by -1 reverses the inequality sign, yielding x < 5. On a continuous real number line, all real values up to 5 (such as 4.99) are valid solutions, which must be represented with an open circle at 5 pointing left. Placing a solid dot at 4 mistakenly excludes infinitely many fractional and decimal solutions between 4 and 5.

suggestedQuestions: What must you do to the inequality sign when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number?
If x is a real number satisfying x < 5, why would placing a solid dot at 4 leave out numbers like 4.8 or 4.999?
If an algebraic step yields 3 < x, why does the ray on the number line point to the right even though '<' points to the left?

nodes.label: Isolate the Variable
nodes.details: Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other using standard inverse operations.

nodes.label: Negative Factor Rule
nodes.details: Reverse the inequality symbol whenever you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number.

nodes.label: Plot Boundary Circle
nodes.details: Place an open circle if the boundary point is excluded, or a solid closed circle if it is included in the solution.

key-properties-of-solving-linear-inequal.title: Solving Linear Inequalities & Graphing Properties

nodes.label: Algebraic Balance Steps
nodes.details: Add or subtract the same quantity from both sides to isolate the variable without altering the inequality sign.

nodes.label: Negative Flip Property
nodes.details: Reverses the direction of the inequality sign whenever both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number.

nodes.label: Circle Endpoint Style
nodes.details: Draw an open circle for strict inequalities (<, >) and a solid circle when the boundary is included (≤, ≥).

nodes.label: Directional Ray Shading
nodes.details: Draw a shaded ray pointing left for smaller values and pointing right for greater values to show all valid solutions.
